No, that isn't right, and it's worth catching now. A language model doesn't remember earlier conversations on its own. Your makerspace assistant won't remember what a student told it last week unless you build that in.

**Example:** A student says on Monday, "I finished the laser cutter training." On the next Monday they open a new chat and ask, "Can I book the laser cutter?" The model only reads the text it is given for that request, which is called its **context**. Last week's chat isn't in that text, so the model has no idea about the training.

It's an easy mistake to make. Chatbots like ChatGPT seem to remember you, but that's because the app around the model saves things and pastes them back into the context. The model itself starts fresh each time.

**What this means for your design:** memory is something your code does.
1. Save the facts that matter, such as "Sam: laser cutter training done, Oct 12", in a file or database.
2. At the start of the next session, look up that student's record.
3. Put it into the context before the model answers.

Which facts to save and how much to load back are your decisions. Both affect cost, because everything in the context is paid for on every request. This is the "what to keep in context and what to save between sessions" part of your mission.

Quick check: a student's training status will be stored in a database. In your own words, what has to happen before the model can use it when answering "Can I book the laser cutter?"

If you'd like, I can turn this into a short lesson on context and memory. It's the next step on your list.
